--- title: "The same random-intercept ML model in R, Python and PHP" jupyter: python3 --- The [math walkthrough](lmm-math.qmd) derives the marginal Gaussian likelihood, group whitening, variance profiling and shrunken conditional group estimates. All runtimes fit the same fixed columns, retained observations and grouping IDs. ::: {#6592c45c .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from pathlib import Path import sys import pandas as pd ROOT=next(p for p in [Path.cwd(),*Path.cwd().parents] if (p/'Cargo.toml').exists()) sys.path.insert(0,str(ROOT/'docs/verifications')) from compare_lmm import cases,compare_case results=[compare_case(c) for c in cases()] first=results[0] print(first['versions']) rows=[] for implementation in ['R','Python','phit']: fit=first[implementation] for j,label in enumerate(['intercept','study hours','prior score']): rows.append(dict(implementation=implementation,term=label,estimate=fit['coefficients'][j],SE=fit['std_errors'][j],z=fit['z_statistics'][j],p=fit['p_values'][j],lower95=fit['conf_int'][j][0],upper95=fit['conf_int'][j][1])) display(pd.DataFrame(rows)) display(pd.DataFrame([dict(case=r['name'],Python_backend=r['python_diagnostics']['backend'], max_absolute_difference_vs_R=max(e for values in r['max_absolute_errors_vs_R'].values() for e in values.values()), PHP_boundary=r['phit']['boundary'],missing_warnings=len(r['warnings'])) for r in results])) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` {'R': 'R version 4.6.1 (2026-06-24)', 'lme4': '2.0.6', 'statsmodels': '0.15.0', 'PHP': '8.5.10', 'Python': '3.14.7'} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Comparisons include every fitted value/residual, fixed-effect inference, group effects, variance components, ICC and marginal likelihood at tolerance 1e-7 + 1e-6 × abs(reference). Group labels, deletion positions and counts are checked exactly. Optimizer evaluation counts are not expected to match. ## Equivalent model calls ```r library(lme4) students <- read.csv('docs/data/schools.csv') fit <- lmer(score ~ study_hours + prior_score + (1|school), data=students, REML=FALSE, control=lmerControl(optimizer='bobyqa',optCtrl=list(rhoend=1e-10))) fixef(fit) vcov(fit) ranef(fit) ``` ```python import statsmodels.api as sm students = pd.read_csv('docs/data/schools.csv') x = sm.add_constant(students[['study_hours','prior_score']]) fit = sm.MixedLM(students.score, x, groups=students.school).fit( reml=False, method='bfgs', gtol=1e-10, maxiter=1000) fit.fe_params, fit.scale, fit.cov_re ``` ```php $x = $y = $groups = []; foreach ($students as $student) { $x[] = [1.0, $student['study_hours'], $student['prior_score']]; $y[] = $student['score']; $groups[] = $student['school']; } $result = Phit\fit_mixed_gaussian_intercept_matrix( x: $x, y: $y, groups: $groups, intercept: false, ); ``` These PHP records are numeric; `examples/lmm.php` has the complete CSV conversion with predictor-only x and an automatic fixed intercept. This comparison passes an explicit design with `intercept: false`, and the runner gives R the same design columns as `y ~ 0 + x0 + ... + (1|group)`. Applications can use `fit_mixed_gaussian()` with a formula instead; see [Mixed models](../mixed-models.qmd). ## Conventions that must match ML is explicit: R and statsmodels otherwise support/default to REML, which fits a different variance criterion. Likelihood here integrates over group effects. Fixed-effect standard errors use plug-in GLS covariance (X' V^-1 X)^-1, matching lme4. statsmodels' reported joint observed-Hessian covariance can differ, so the Python runner explicitly recalculates the declared GLS convention using its fitted variance components; it does not claim its unmodified bse_fe matches every case. Normal z-based Wald intervals are constructed explicitly for every reference. Our df_residual=n-p is informational. R mixed-model df methods may include the two variance parameters; no finite-sample t degrees of freedom are claimed here. AIC counts p+2 parameters in every case, including a zero variance boundary. The exact tau²=0 fixture is checked against lme4 and PHP, with a separately labeled NumPy OLS-limit reference. It is not represented as a converged statsmodels mixed fit. At this boundary, variance is RSS/n and standard errors differ from OLS's unbiased-scale inference. This explicit check avoids treating an approximate positive-variance optimizer solution as proof of exact boundary behavior. ::: {#3309634e .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} keys=['residual_variance','random_intercept_variance','icc','log_likelihood','aic'] display(pd.DataFrame([dict(implementation=name,**{k:first[name][k] for k in keys}) for name in ['R','Python','phit']])) print('Python fit warnings:', first['python_diagnostics']['warnings']) missing=results[-1] print('Dropped original rows:',missing['phit']['dropped_rows']) print('Missing-data warning:',missing['warnings']) print('Schools and effects:',list(zip(first['phit']['group_labels'],first['phit']['random_effects']))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
